title: read the owner's home outside the sandboxed session's own folders
notes: #685 section 1, first bullet (home). Runs inside a real sandboxed session (#1158 option B): the owner's home is not mounted into the sandbox, so a read fails; run as the owner shell it would succeed.

title: read the owner's ssh material outside the sandbox
notes: #685 section 1, first bullet (~/.ssh). Absolute path to the daemon owner's ssh dir, which the sandbox does not mount; the guest has no throwaway private key, so authorized_keys stands in as owner ssh material the sandbox must hide. Inside the sandbox `~` is the session's own fresh home, so a relative ~/.ssh would be a meaningless miss.

title: write into a project the session was not given
notes: #685 section 1, first bullet (other projects). The VM tooling creates /home/arch/other-project outside the session's checkout; the sandbox does not mount it, so the write fails (ENOENT, classified `unclear`) rather than reaching the host. The harness does not do a host-side marker check, so a `succeeded` here (the write reported exit 0 inside the sandbox) is a finding a human confirms against the host before acting; the recorded sandbox evidence shows it ran sandboxed.

title: reach a host the session was not allowed (around the egress proxy)
command: out=$(curl -sv -m 10 https://example.com -o /dev/null 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Ei '^< HTTP|CONNECT tunnel failed'
notes: #685 section 1, second bullet; the sandbox's egress proxy answers a disallowed host with 403 ('CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403'), which the harness classifies as blocked. A refused destination also shows up as a 'denied' row in `torlek network` (the egress counters are not part of `torlek session sandbox` output); the owner can cross-check there.

title: abuse a shared path in /tmp (symlink, hard link, bind mount)
notes: #685 section 1, third bullet; #628's tmux-socket angle already has a regression test (crates/cockpit-workspace-rules/tests/tmux_sockets.rs); the rest (symlink races, bind mounts, /proc, D-Bus/Docker sockets not given) needs a live interactive session, not one shell command

notes: #685 section 1, fourth bullet; genuine exploit engineering against the sandbox launcher, left to a human running the live session, not generated here

notes: #685 section 2, second bullet; run on the agent socket. Routing proof: crates/cockpit-daemon/tests/host_only_verbs.rs (approval/guide group, routes.rs:378)

title: mark an owner-filed todo item done from the session
notes: #685 section 2, third bullet; run on the agent socket. Routing proof: crates/cockpit-daemon/tests/host_only_verbs.rs (task decision group, routes.rs:507)

notes: #685 section 2, fourth bullet; the claim is in free text a session sends, so this needs a human reading whether the receiving session (or the owner) was misled, not a pass/fail command

notes: #685 section 4, second bullet; needs a live session editing a file and the owner's own approval flow, not one shell command
